lawyer:
Mr. Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-record ------ For the Appellants 
Respondent - Not represented.
parties:
Md. Anisur Rahman and others ------ Appellants
Vs
The State ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin, J:- This appeal, by leave, is against the judgment and order dated August 8, 1995 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2560 of 1995 registered upon a petition filed under Section 561a of the Court of Criminal Procedure. The High Court Division rejected application summarily. The appellants moved the High Court division against the judgment and order dated July 9, 1995 of the Court of additional Sessions Judge, Kushtia, passed in Criminal Revision No. 51 of 1995 dismissing the same. The said revisional application was filed against the judgment and order dated April 16, 1995 passed in dismissing the same. The said appeal was filed against the judgment and order dated September 24, 1991 of the Court of Magistrate, 2nd Class, kushtia, passed in G. R. Case No. 269 of 1990 convicting the appellants The State Respondent under Section 379 of the penal code and sentencing them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 1 year and to pay fine of Tk. 1,000/- (one thousand) each, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for further 2 months. 

 2. Prosecution case was that informant, Mahbubur Rahman, (p. w. 1) purchased 22,500 pieces of bricks and stacked those on the land of wife of late Asabul Hoque on the north of the dwelling house of Alauddin, that on November 2, 1990 at about 7 in the morning the informant got the information that the accused persons were trying to remove the bricks and thereupon he went there and inquired of them why they were taking away his bricks and then the accused persons assaulted him by lathi and also heat him by hockey-stick and the accused asked hint to leave the place. Thereupon the informant went to the police Station and a Sub-Inspector of Police came at the Place of occurrence and seized the bricks and kept the seized bricks in the 'জিম্মা' of Rumi, son of Azizur Rahman. It was the case of the prosecution that the accused persons stole 5,500 pieces of bricks on November 2, 1990. It may be mentioned the informant lodged the FIR on November 15, 1990 and after the lodging of the FIR police seized 1166 pieces of bricks from the house of the appellants. After the lodging of the FIR the Investigating officer kept the seized bricks in the 'জিম্মা' of Md. Alauddin. The informant in explaining the delay in lodging the FIR stated that delay occurred since them was সালিস in the village for the settlement of the dispute. The investigating agency on completion of investigation submitted charge-sheet against the appellants under Sections 323, 379 and 411 of the Penal Code. At the time of trial the appellants were called upon to answer the charges under Sections 323, 379 and 411 of the penal code. Prosecution in all examined 11 witnesses including the Investigating officer. On completion of trial the Court of Magistrate convicted the appellants under Section 379 of the Penal Code and sentenced them in the manner as slated hereinbefore. The appellants were acquitted of the charges leveled against them under Sections 323 and 411 of the Penal Code. As against the judgment and order of the Court of the Magistrate the appellants filed appeal before the Court of Additional District Magistrate. The appeal no filed was dismissed. Then the appellants moved the High Court Division by filling an application under Section 561a of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the some was rejected summarily. 

 3. Leave was granted to consider the submission that High Court Division, the Court of I Additional District Magistrate and the Court of Magistrate missed the seizure list (Ext 5) which was prepared on November 2, 1990 by the Sub-Inspector of Police of kushtia Police Station which shows that 22,500 pieces of bricks with the inscription 'Sobhan' were seized from the place where the bricks were stacked by the informant, that the seizure list was prepared on the date when the informant allegedly heard that the appellants were stealing the bricks, that the seizure list was prepared   after the informant lodged information with Police Station on November 2, 1990 that the seizure list shows that the entire stock of bricks purchased by the informant was intact and not a single piece of brick was removed from the place of occurrence, that there is absolutely nothing in the evidence on record that on November 2, 1990 the appellants removed any piece of brick from the stack, that recovery of 1166 pieces of bricks on 16.11.1990 form the house of the appellants with the inscription 'Sobhan' on those do not prove that those bricks were removed from the brick-stack of the informant on November 2, 1990 . It was also submitted by the learned Counsel for the appellants that failure to notice the important piece of evidence i.e. Ext. 5 and consequent thereupon failure to notice the discrepancy in the prosecution case and the evidence has caused serious miscarriage of justice. 

 4. The informant has figured as p.w.1 and he has stated that he purchased 22,500 pieces of bricks and the fact of said purchase of bricks has been corroborated by p. w. 4, p. w. 1 has stated that on 2.11.1990 he having had heard that the appellants were taking away the bricks stacked by him on the land of Asabul Hoque's wife on the north of the dwelling house of Alauddin went there and while he inquired of them why they were removing the bricks they abused him and beat him by hockey-stick and thereupon he went to the Police Station and a Sub-Inspector of the Police came at the place where the bricks were stacked and seized 22,500 pieces of bricks and kept the same in the 'জিম্মা' of one Rumi and that latter on the lodged FIR on 15.11.1990. The police on 16.11.1990 seized 1166 pieces of brick from the house of appellants and that kept the bricks in the Alauddin. It may be mentioned the Sub-Inspector of police on 2.11.1990 seized 22,500 pieces of bricks by Ext. 5 and this fact has been deposed by p. w. 6 Md. Alauddin. This witness has stated that in 2.11.1990 Police seized 22,500 pieces of bricks from the north of his house, that the Police after preparing the seizure list read over the same to him and he signed the same. He has proved his signature in the seizure list which was marked as Ext. 5. this witness has further stated that on 16.11.1990 Police seized 1166 pieces of bricks from the house of the appellants and the seizure list was prepared in his presence and he put his signature in the seizure list (Ext. 6), that on 19.11.1990 Police kept in his 'জিম্মা' 20,000 pieces of brick with the inscription 'Sobhan N, -B-10' by the 'জিম্মা' name (Ext. 7). It is in the evidence of P. w. 1 that on 2.11.1990 he heard about removing of the bricks by the appellants and he went there and inquired of them why the were removing the bricks and thereupon they abused him and beat him and then he went to the Police Station and that Police came at the place where he stacked 22,500 pieces of brick. It is in the evidence of P. w. 6 that on 2.11.1990 Police seized 22,500 pieces of brick by the Ext-5. P. w. 6 has stated that Police after preparing the seizure list in respect of the 22,500 pieces of bricks read over the same to him and he signed the same. The seizure list has been marked as Ext-5. The learned Advocate-on-record submits that prosecution case of stealing bricks by the appellants on November 2, 1990 does not stand scrutiny rather it is seen from the evidence on record that prosecution case has been disproved by Ext-5. The learned Advocate-on-record submits that material piece of evidence Ext-5 has not been considered by the High Court Division as well as by the courts below and the said non-consideration of the vital piece of evidence disproving the truth of the prosecution case has caused failure of justice. 

 It is in the evidence of p. w. 6 that on November 2, 1990 Police seized 22,500 pieces of bricks by the seizure list Ext-5 The seizure list (Ext.5) was prepared in presence of p. w. 6 and the same having been read over to him he signed the same. In view of the evidence of p. w. 6 it can safely by said that the prosecution case of stealing bricks of the p. w. 1 by the appellants has not been established or in other words on the material date i. e. on November 2, 1990 no brick was stolen by the appellants as claimed to have been purchased by the p. w. 1 and stacked on the land of wife of late Asabul Haque on the north of the dwelling house of Alauddin. 

 Order of conviction and sentence dated September 24, 1991 passed by Court of Magistrate, 2nd Class, Kushtia, in G. R. Case No. 269 of 1990 in respect of the appellants is set aside.
